contentSections: Curtain wall and rainscreen are two of the most common facade systems on Indian buildings, yet many clients mix them up. Both hang on the outside of the structure. Both can look sleek. But they work in very different ways, cost differently and suit different buildings. This guide explains each system in plain English, compares them side by side and helps you decide which fits your building and budget.
The Short Answer

• Curtain wall is a lightweight, non load bearing outer skin, usually glass in an aluminium frame, that hangs from the building structure. It is mostly about daylight, views and a glazed look.
  • Rainscreen cladding is an outer layer of panels, such as metal, fixed with a ventilated gap in front of a weatherproof wall. It is mostly about protection, performance and design variety.
  • Many buildings use both: curtain wall where daylight matters, rainscreen on solid walls.

What Is a Curtain Wall?

A curtain wall is a facade system that hangs in front of the floor slabs. It does not carry the building's weight, only its own weight and wind loads, which it passes to the structure. Most curtain walls use an aluminium frame with glass infill, though some include opaque panels. Two common types are stick systems, assembled piece by piece on site, and unitised systems, built in factory as large units and lifted into place. Curtain walls are the base for the glass towers you see in every Indian metro. Read how glass compares with metal in our guide on glass facade vs metal facade.

What Is Rainscreen Cladding?

Rainscreen cladding is a two layer wall. The outer layer is a panel, often metal, fixed on brackets and rails. Behind it is an air gap, and behind that is the weatherproof wall with insulation. The outer panels stop most rain. The gap lets air move and moisture dry out. Joints between panels are often left open or only partly closed. Because the panels sit off the wall, heat can escape through the cavity. This makes rainscreen especially useful in hot Indian climates. Performance Factors

Heat and Energy

Curtain walls with standard glass let in a lot of solar heat. High performance glazing and external shading reduce this. Rainscreen systems with insulation and a ventilated cavity cut heat reaching the wall. For many Indian buildings, a smart mix of glazing and rainscreen gives the best comfort and energy balance.

Water Tightness

Curtain walls rely on sealed joints, gaskets and drainage inside the frame. Rainscreens rely on the principle that panels deflect most rain, while a membrane and wall behind are the final defence. Both work well when designed and installed correctly. Poor detailing causes leaks in either system.

Fire Safety

Both systems must meet fire rules, including cavity barriers and fire stops. Insulation and panel materials matter. Our guide on fire rated cladding in India covers what reviewers look at.

Noise

Glass curtain walls can transmit more outside noise unless they use laminated or double glazed units. Rainscreen systems over solid walls usually perform better with the right wall build up.

Weight and Structure

Both are lighter than traditional masonry or stone cladding. Panel and frame weight affect the sub-structure design, so your engineer must check it for either system.

Cost: Look Beyond Day One

Cost depends on system type, materials, height, complexity and finish. Instead of comparing a single price per square foot, compare:

1. Supply and installation of the complete system
  2. Energy and cooling impact over 15 to 20 years
  3. Cleaning and access costs
  4. Repair and replacement
  5. Lifespan and refurbishment cost
Our metal facade cost in India guide explains what drives price.
When Curtain Wall Fits Best

• Corporate offices that need daylight and views
  • Lobbies, atriums and showroom fronts
  • Buildings where a glazed, transparent identity is the goal
  • North facing or well shaded elevations
When Rainscreen Fits Best

• Hot, sun facing walls
  • Residences, hospitals, schools and institutional buildings
  • Retrofit of existing buildings
  • Buildings that want a strong design identity with metal panels
  • Projects with tight upkeep budgets

Combining Both

Most modern buildings mix systems. Curtain wall may run across the lobby and office floors, while rainscreen panels wrap the core, service floors and sun facing walls. This puts glass where people need light and metal where the building needs protection. For help choosing the right system, read how to choose the right facade cladding system and our guide to facade systems explained.
Questions to Ask Before You Decide

• What are the daylight needs of each floor?
  • Which elevations get the harshest sun?
  • What are the fire and code requirements for this building?
  • What is the lifetime budget, including cleaning and repair?
  • Is this a new build or a retrofit?
  • What does the facade need to say about the building?
Common Mistakes

• Choosing curtain wall everywhere for looks, then paying for cooling and cleaning
  • Choosing rainscreen without planning the cavity, membrane and fire stops
  • Comparing prices without comparing scope
  • Ignoring upkeep access in the design
  • Skipping mock-ups and testing
Frequently Asked Questions

Is a rainscreen the same as cladding?

Rainscreen is a type of cladding system with a ventilated gap behind the outer panels.

Is curtain wall cheaper than rainscreen?

It depends on glass and panel specification. High performance curtain walls can be costly, while rainscreen cost varies with the panel material.

Which is better for heat in India?

Rainscreen with a ventilated cavity usually handles heat better than unshaded glass curtain wall.

Can I combine curtain wall and rainscreen?

Yes. Many buildings use both.

Can rainscreen be used on an existing building?

Often yes, with a structural check and a proper sub-frame.
